sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Anti-HA antibody staining of intact HEK293T cells confirmed surface display by flow cytometry. Endogenous CLEC14A function was not independently assayed in this construct; the construct was used as a positive-control reagent to validate anti-CLEC14A monoclonal antibodies (clones C2 and C4).
sites.rationale: The construct is named 'HA-CLEC14A', indicating an N-terminal HA tag. CLEC14A has a signal peptide spanning residues 1–21 (landmarks, authoritative); a tag placed upstream of residue 22 would be co-translationally cleaved with the signal peptide and lost. The only viable extracellular N-terminal junction is therefore after residue 21 (G) and before residue 22 (E), the mature N-terminus. Python verification confirms seq[20]='G' and seq[21]='E', and the mature N-terminus is 376 residues from the TM boundary (398), well beyond the ≥3-residue constraint. No residue number was stated in the paper, so position_evidence is topology_derived. HEK293T cells stably overexpressing an HA-CLEC14A construct (N-terminal HA tag, exact junction residue not stated in the paper) were stained with anti-HA antibody and confirmed to display the tag on the cell surface by flow cytometry. CLEC14A is a single-pass type I transmembrane protein; its only extracellular terminus is the mature N-terminus beginning at residue 22 (signal peptide 1–21 is cleaved). The HA tag must therefore reside between the signal peptide cleavage site and residue 22.

sources.claim: To confirm the clones could recognise cell bound CLEC14A, HEK293T cells overexpressing HA-CLEC14A were stained with clone C2 or C4 or a monoclonal HA tag antibody.

literature_notes: Only one ledger line (L1) was provided. It reports an HA-CLEC14A construct with surface display confirmed by flow cytometry in HEK293T cells. The paper does not state the exact junction residue, but CLEC14A is a single-pass type I TM protein with a single extracellular terminus (mature N-terminus, residue 22), making the position unambiguous by topology. No internal extracellular loop insertions, C-terminal tags, or other positions are supported by the ledger. The C-terminus (residues 419–490) is intracellular and was not reported as tagged. No abrogating or intracellular positions were reported in the ledger.
